newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-ELS WINS BUICK WIRE TO WIRE FOR SECOND YEAR.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ELS WINS BUICK WIRE TO WIRE FOR SECOND YEAR.

text.p: U.S. Open champion Ernie Els scored his second successive wire-to-wire Buick Open victory by shooting a two-under-par 69 in the final round Sunday to hold off a familiar rival, Jeff Maggert.
Els at 16-under-par 268 finished two strokes ahead of Maggert, whose three-under 68 left him in second place behind the South African for the second year in a row at Westchester Country Club.
Maggert also battled Els down the stretch in the Open at Congressional last week before stumbling at the end and finishing fourth.
Els has held the lead at Westchester for eight straight rounds. He is a collective 46 under par for the four tournaments he has played here.
"If there are horses for courses, this is probably my golf course," said Els. "Obviously, I love the place. It's a great feeling to win here again."

Last year, Els won by eight strokes, and this time on Saturday afternoon it appeared he could better that. Eight shots clear of the field after 12 holes on Saturday, Els saw that margin dwindle to just one stroke 10 holes later.
Els was one ahead of Maggert after four holes in the final round when brief but severe thundershowers interrupted play for two hours.

"At the break my lead was down to one, which may have been a blessing in disguise because it made me think about what I had to do. I decided to make pars and make them come to me, and as it turned out, I made the right choice to play conservatively," said Els.

Maggert, who putted beautifully when he needed to save par all day, missed a six-footer for birdie on the seventh hole which would have tied him with Els. It was the closest Maggert would get to catching him. "Ernie just didn't make any mistakes," said Maggert.

On the 18th green the South African's lead was two strokes and both men were putting for eagle from about 30 feet. Els went first, lagging his putt to virtual tap-in range so that even if Maggert were to sink his eagle putt it almost certainly would not force a play-off.

After both had made their birdies, Maggert playfully grabbed Els and briefly tussled with him. "I was trying to shove him down into the green and smash him. But he's pretty big and I couldn't take him down," said the usually soft-spoken Maggert with a grin.

Maggert has won only once in his seven-year career, but has finished second nine times. "It's no fun to play well and finish second. Well, it is fun to play well, but it gets tiresome coming up short.

"Last week I felt very negative leaving, but this week was a proving ground and now I know I'm playing well. I want to make the Ryder Cup team, and I expect to make it the way I'm playing," said Maggert.

The win for Els, the fifth of his PGA Tour career and his 21st worldwide, was worth $270,000. It also propelled him to the top spot in the world rankings, supplanting Tiger Woods, who had replaced Greg Norman just last week.

"It's quite a surprise. I don't know what to say about it. I struggle for six months and win two tournaments and am the number one. But right at this exact moment, yes, I probably am number one. I've never said that before," said Els.
Woods shot a one-over-par 72 Sunday to finish at three-over 287, tied for 43rd. Woods, who has played five of the last six weeks, has broken par just once in his last 12 rounds.

The competition has tired him, and the unrelenting attention has wearied him even more. Woods plans to spend a week at home in Florida doing a lot of fishing and little golf. "I've run myself into the ground," he said.

Woods's round included two of the double bogeys which have made too frequent appearances on his cards recently, but it also included a four-iron to two feet on the par-five fifth hole that allowed him to tap in for eagle.

Woods also drove the green at the par-four 10th and two-putted for birdie. "I didn't play that well, but I learned a lot about my game. It's not quite there, but I made good improvement this week, though my scores didn't show it."
Woods is scheduled to return to competition at the Western Open, July 3-6, and is giving another youth clinic in Chicago on June 30.
